text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City Policy or by-laws. Transportation Services is reporting on the results of the traffic calming poll undertaken on Hilton Avenue, between Melgund Road and Nina Street. The poll provided a response rate of less than 50 percent plus one ballot required by the traffic calming policy needed to confirm that there is a favourable consensus in the community to install traffic calming measure. Accordingly, continuing the process to install speed humps on Hilton Avenue, between Melgund Road and Nina Street, is not recommended.

The Toronto and East York Community Council directed: 1. The City Solicitor prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install three speed humps on Hilton Avenue, between Melgund Road and Nina Street, generally as shown on Drawing No. 421G-2989, dated May 2018 attached to the report entitled "Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) Poll Results - Hilton Avenue" from the Acting Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services.
